transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, because I know everyone gets tired, but... well, what brings me in is that I've just been so exhausted lately. 

And it's in this way that sleep just doesn't seem to fix? I mean, I'm still getting my job done—I manage a team, so I always make sure to keep things running smoothly—but just getting through a normal workday, and then trying to do dinner at home... it just feels so much heavier than it really should. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm explaining that right. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little? I really try not to complain, because I know I have so much to be grateful for, but... yeah. Most days lately, I wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's sort of like I'm already disappointed in the day before it even really starts. 

I mean, I always push past it and put on a good face for my team, of course, but it's just kind of there in the background making everything harder. I hope it's okay to admit that. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you find yourself enjoying things you normally like to do, or has that changed lately?

Well, um... I guess that's changed a little bit, too. I mean, I usually love painting—watercolors, mostly—and I really enjoy wandering through museum exhibits on the weekends. It's usually my way to unwind. But recently... I don't know, I just leave my supplies sitting there untouched. 

And I've seen a few exhibits advertised that I know I'd normally be thrilled to go see, but I just... I can't seem to make myself care enough to actually go. I feel terrible saying that, because I know I should be keeping up with my hobbies, and I really don't want to sound lazy. I'm still keeping up with all my responsibilities, I promise! It's just the fun stuff that's kind of... dropped off. Is that normal when you're feeling this tired?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Oh, um... well, like I was just mentioning with my watercolors and the museum exhibits... I really wish I had a better answer for you. I keep hoping I'll wake up and want to pick up my brushes again, or feel that spark to go out and see something new, but... right now, it's just really hard to find that joy in much of anything. 

I do try, I really do! I'll sit there and try to force myself to be interested, but it just feels a bit blank. I'm sorry, I know that sounds so gloomy, and I promise I'm usually a very upbeat person! I just... I guess I don't really have anything I'm looking forward to right now. I hope it's alright that I don't have a better answer for you?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, it's nothing to worry about, really! I've just been... well, picking at my meals a bit more than usual. And sometimes I get so caught up with things at work that I just sort of... forget to eat lunch. 

It's not that I'm trying to starve myself or anything, I promise! I know how important it is to eat right. But I did notice that a few of my work skirts are fitting a little looser lately, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight. I hope that's not too concerning? I'm sure my appetite will bounce back soon once I get a little more energy!
Have you been feeling anxious or nervous lately?

Oh, anxious? Um... not really, no. I mean, I guess everyone gets a little stressed out sometimes, right? With work and everything, being a manager means there's always something to juggle. But I wouldn't say I'm nervous or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a level head and not let things get to me. I know it's not good to be all wound up, so I try to just take things in stride. I haven't been feeling panicky or anything, I promise! Just the normal day-to-day stuff. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Oh, um... well, let me think. I guess this current patch—feeling so low and just sort of empty—has been going on for about a month now. 

Before that, I was actually doing really well! I had so much energy, and I was getting so much done at work, maybe even a little unusually driven, you know? I felt fantastic. But then it just sort of... shifted, and I've been stuck in this slump for the last four weeks or so. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is! It's just a little phase, I'm sure. Is it normal for things to swing like that?
Have you been having any thoughts about death or wanting to hurt yourself?

Oh, goodness, no! No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I know sometimes people get really down and have those kinds of dark thoughts, but that's definitely not me. I promise! 

I mean, sure, I've been feeling a bit sluggish and down, like I said, but I would never... I don't think about hurting myself or anything drastic like that. I have too much going on at work, and I really try to stay positive even when I'm in a slump. I know it's just a phase, and I just need to push through it, right? I really hope you don't think I'm that bad off! I'm doing my best to keep everything together. Does that sound okay?
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt completely fine and your normal self?

Well, um... completely fine? I try really hard to have good days, I really do. But, um... if I'm being totally honest, maybe not really? 

Most days lately, I just kind of wake up with this... this heavy, gray feeling. It's almost like I'm already disappointed in the day before it even really starts, if that makes sense. I mean, I still get up and go to the office and get everything done! I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or anything. I always make sure to put on a smile for my team and get my work finished. But underneath, it's just been a bit of a struggle to feel like my usual, cheerful self. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much!
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately?

Oh, well... maybe just a tiny bit? I definitely don't want it to sound like I'm dragging myself around the office or anything dramatic like that! But, um... my staff actually pointed out something recently. 

They noticed I’ve been a little slower to answer questions in our team meetings. It’s just... it's like there’s this little pause before I can get my thoughts and my words moving, if that makes sense? I'm still handling all my managerial duties and leading the meetings, I promise! It just takes me an extra second to gather my thoughts right now. I really hope they don't think I'm doing a bad job... Is it normal to get a little delayed like that when you're feeling down?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Oh, um, well... I haven't been on a diet or anything! I really try to make sure I'm taking care of myself. But, um... I guess I have noticed my skirts are fitting just a little bit looser lately. 

It's nothing serious, I promise! I think I've just been... well, picking at my meals a bit more. And sometimes, with everything going on at the office, I just sort of forget to eat lunch. I'm still eating, though! Just maybe not quite as much as I usually do. It's not like I'm starving myself or anything, I just haven't had much of an appetite. Is that okay? I mean, a little weight loss isn't the worst thing, right?
Have you felt like you're moving more slowly than usual lately?

Oh, um... I know I just mentioned that little delay with my speaking in meetings, but... did you mean like physically moving my body? Like walking around? 

If you mean physically, I really don't think I'm moving any slower. I always make sure to keep a good, brisk pace around the office! I definitely wouldn't want anyone to see me just sort of dragging my feet down the hallway or anything like that. So physically, no, I haven't really noticed any changes. I'm still trying my best to stay on top of everything and look energetic for the team. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I'm sorry if I misunderstood or if I'm just repeating myself! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had any difficulty concentrating on things like reading or watching TV?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm having trouble with reading or TV or anything like that! I still watch my evening shows to unwind, and that's perfectly fine. But, um... I guess I have noticed a tiny little issue at work? 

It's really nothing major, I'm still getting everything done! But sometimes, I'll be looking at a really simple staffing email, and... well, I'll just sit there and reread it a few times. It's like I just can't quite decide what to say or which option makes the most sense right in that moment. I think I'm just wanting to make sure I make the right decision for the team, you know? Being thorough! 

I eventually figure it out, of course! It just takes me a little longer to process it than it usually would. I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm slipping at my job... it's normal to get a little stuck on emails sometimes, right?
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt almost no depressive symptoms at all?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I've been trying so hard to stay positive, I really have! But if I'm being completely honest, I don't think I've had a day where I felt totally, completely fine in the last couple of weeks. 

It's just this... this sort of heaviness that's always kind of there in the background, even when I'm smiling through a meeting. I try not to let it show, and I'm definitely still functioning and doing everything I need to do! But... yeah, I haven't had a day where it was just entirely gone. 

Is it bad that I haven't been able to just shake it off for a day? I really am trying to push through it, I promise.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in?

Oh, um... well, I'm still keeping up with all my work responsibilities and everything I need to do for others, of course! I always make sure to show up when people need me. But, um... I guess when it comes to my own personal downtime... 

I usually absolutely love painting. And I normally spend my weekends wandering through different museum exhibits—it's always been my favorite way to recharge. But recently... I don't know, I just leave my art supplies sitting there completely untouched. And even when there's a new exhibit in town that I know I'd normally be thrilled to see, I just... I can't seem to make myself care enough to actually go. 

It's probably just because I've been dedicating so much energy to my job, right? I'm sure I'll get back to it all soon! I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or uncultured... it's perfectly fine to take a little break from hobbies sometimes, isn't it?
How many days in the past month have you felt this heavy, gray feeling?

Oh, um... I guess I'd have to say most days, if I'm looking back at the whole month. I really hate to admit that, because I know I have so much to be thankful for, and I always try to focus on the positive! 

But, um... yeah, most days lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It's almost like... well, like I'm already disappointed in the day before it even starts? Which sounds so pessimistic, and I promise I'm usually a very upbeat person! I still get right out of bed and make sure my team has everything they need for the morning, of course. I'd never let it affect them. 

But... it's just been there most mornings recently. That's fairly common when you're just a bit run down, right? I'm sure everyone wakes up feeling a little unmotivated like that sometimes...
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt almost no depressive symptoms at all, but if you did, were they at the beginning, middle, or end of the month?

Oh, um... well, earlier in the month was actually quite different! I wouldn't call it depressive at all. Actually, I felt, um... really quite wonderful for a few days right at the beginning of the month. 

I was just so upbeat and, I don't know, charged up? I felt like I had all these brilliant ideas for the house and my team at work. I was getting so much done! But, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, I might have been a little... difficult to be around? 

My husband just asked a simple question about one of my projects, and I got so unusually irritated with him, so fast. Which is terrible of me, I know! I usually never snap at him like that. I'm sure I was just overtired from being so productive, right? It's normal to get a little snappy when you're just really focused and passionate about your plans, isn't it?
How many consecutive days have you been feeling this heavy, gray feeling without any significant improvement?

Oh, um... well, it's been about a month now, I suppose. Ever since those few really energetic, driven days at the beginning of the month ended, it's just been... this constant low feeling. 

I really try not to let it get to me, and I make sure I'm still smiling for everyone at the office! But, um... yeah, it's been about a solid month of this heavy feeling without much of a break. I feel terrible complaining about it, because I know a month isn't really that long in the grand scheme of things, is it? I'm sure it's just a little phase that will pass soon, right?
Have you been feeling this heavy, gray feeling for more than two weeks without any letup?

Oh, um... yes, definitely more than two weeks. I know I just mentioned it a second ago, and I really hate to sound like a broken record! I promise I'm not usually someone who just sits around complaining. 

But, um... yes, this recent swing—from being so unusually energized and driven to just... persistently low—it’s been going on for about a month now. Without any real letup, unfortunately. But I'm still keeping up with my team at work and making sure everything runs smoothly! So it's not completely unmanageable. That's a good sign, isn't it?
Do you feel your depressive symptoms are interfering with your daily life?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say it's completely interfering, no! I mean, I'm still showing up for work every day, and I'm making sure everything at home is taken care of. I really pride myself on being dependable. 

But... I guess if I'm being totally honest, I have been a little... slower? Like, making decisions at work takes me twice as long right now. And I might have canceled on a few family plans lately, which I feel just awful about! I hate letting people down. I've also sort of stopped going to my weekend art classes, which I usually love... I just haven't had the energy. 

But I'm still managing the important things! Everyone gets a little behind sometimes when they're not feeling their best, right? It's not like I'm falling apart or anything. I'm sure I'm just needing a little more rest than usual, don't you think?
